clue.text: Colourful material Christopher and Jack rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the run of letters for the two names is read from the end

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: Two men named Christopher and Jack turn down some brightly coloured cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole run KITAB backwards. Christopher and Jack look like two people, but they are a name and a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is wax-resist dyed fabric, typically richly patterned and colourful.

clue.text: Help for Jack to rise, as blanket is pulled off

indicators.note: a blanket pulled off is torn about and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is dragged out of bed by having the blanket yanked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled off' rearranges AS BLANKET; 'is' is a link. Jack climbs the giant beanstalk in the fairy tale, so it helps him go up.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale Jack climbs a giant plant stem to reach the giant's castle.

clue.text: Gradually reduce light

definitions.meaning: to narrow or diminish little by little
a slender candle or wick used to give a flame

explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to thin off progressively; a taper is also a thin candle used for lighting.

clue.text: Cast-off clothing

parts.note: reads as discarded secondhand clothes, but casting off is the final step in knitting a garment from needles

explanation.definitionFit: Garments made with needles and yarn are finished by casting off the stitches.

clue.text: Want a little snow or rain?

explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a want of something; read in two words it is a brief bout of precipitation.

clue.text: Change and put feet up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upward, so read backwards

parts.note: an animal's feet are its paws

explanation.surface: Someone changes position and rests their feet on a stool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PAWS round in this down clue; 'and put' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is to make a change.

clue.text: Roof is provided free

definitions.meaning: where a roof sits: atop a building
given at no charge, paid for by the establishment

explanation.definitionFit: A roof sits atop a home; drinks given at the bar's expense are complimentary in the same idiom.

clue.text: Instrument used to start nursery rhyme about naughty child

definitions.text: used to start nursery rhyme about naughty child
definitions.meaning: the opening words of the rhyme about the piper's son who stole a pig and ran away

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son' is a traditional English children's verse about a boy who steals a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of drum, and the repeated name opens the rhyme 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son'.

clue.text: Powerful spirit used in port

definitions.meaning: a White Sea port in northern Russia, Arkhangelsk in Russian

explanation.definitionFit: A chief angel such as Michael or Gabriel is a mighty spirit; the Russian port bears the same name.

clue.text: Weapon costing Arthur's knight a fortune?

definitions.text: Weapon costing Arthur's knight a fortune?

parts.words: Weapon costing Arthur's knight a fortune?
parts.note: the name of Guinevere's lover at the Round Table, split as a spear-like arm plus 'a lot', reads as a weapon that costs a fortune

explanation.definitionFit: This long spear begins the name of Arthur's chief knight, and the rest of his name reads as costing 'a lot'.

clue.text: Person seeking position, a place I am able to fill in part

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the following words go inside the abbreviation for part, filling its gap

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
I am able means I can

explanation.surface: A job-hunter is told there is a position they can partly fill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill in' is the container signal: the place, I and 'am able' all fill the gap in the part abbreviation. 'Person seeking position' looks like it might continue into the wordplay, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies for a job is seeking a post.

clue.text: Expecting rain in wine-growing area?

parts.note: someone expecting rain has their raincoat on; split differently, that phrase names a Burgundy wine town

explanation.walkthrough: A MAC is British slang for a raincoat (a mackintosh), so wearing one, you have your MAC ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burgundy town of Mâcon gives its name to the surrounding wine district.

clue.text: Careless writing, son — go slowly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
to crawl is to move at a snail's pace

explanation.surface: A parent tells a son with messy handwriting to slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy, hurried handwriting is a hasty illegible scribble.

clue.text: Does wrong, dead miserable

indicators.note: written wrong, the letters of the preceding word come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Someone who does wrong is left utterly wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal on 'Does'. 'dead' looks like an intensifier, as in 'dead miserable', but it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means forlorn and wretched, deeply unhappy.

clue.text: Make quick meal, cooked for Australian to eat

indicators.note: one word swallowing another puts the second inside the first

parts.note: Strine is a humorous name for broad Australian English

indicators.note: food cooked is changed in form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone rustles up a quick meal for a visitor from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals the anagram of 'meal' and 'to eat' the container; 'for' only joins. Strine is a jokey rendering of how Australians say 'Australian'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshape something for less drag, or to simplify it, is to make it faster or more efficient.

clue.text: After a dry run, battle is a draw

indicators.note: the battle word is placed after the preceding pieces in the answer

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who keeps off drink
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
action is fighting in battle

explanation.surface: Following a rehearsal, a fight proves to be a crowd-pleaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the battle last; 'is' only joins. 'dry run' looks like a rehearsal, but splits into two separate pieces, teetotal and the cricket run.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that draws crowds, such as a tourist sight, is a big pull.

clue.text: Challenge story about nobleman and queen

indicators.note: the story word is placed about, round, the nobleman

parts.note: a tale is a story
a lord is a nobleman
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A tale about a lord and a queen is hard to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'and' only joins. R for queen comes from Regina, as in royal cyphers such as ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A daunting task, a demanding request, is a stiff challenge.

clue.text: Not in favour of executing pickpocket

indicators.note: an execution removes the head, so the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Fagin trains child pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: Someone opposes hanging a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executing' beheads FAGIN, removing F; 'of' only joins. AGIN is a dialect form of against.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect word for against, opposed to something.

clue.text: Enjoying Remembrance of Things Past?

parts.note: the title of Proust's novel read literally: taking pleasure in recalling bygone things

explanation.walkthrough: Remembrance of Things Past is the English title of Proust's novel; read literally it describes fond recollection.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful pleasure in remembering former times is a longing for the past.

clue.text: I float at sea — be picked up in this?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked person floats in the water, hoping to be rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges I FLOAT and BE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue vessel is what survivors adrift are hauled aboard.

clue.text: Skirt length fixed in outfit

indicators.note: the length abbreviation is fixed inside the word for outfit

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothing, as a sports team's strip

explanation.surface: The length of a skirt is set as part of an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed in' puts L inside KIT. A kilt is the Scottish pleated skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: This pleated tartan garment worn by Scottish men is a knee-length skirt.

clue.text: Everyone, myself included, breaking into poetry in palace

indicators.note: the group of letters forces its way inside the word for poetry

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry

indicators.note: the speaker is included, put inside the word for everyone

parts.note: all means everyone
I is the speaker, myself

explanation.surface: Everyone, the speaker too, recites poems inside a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' and 'breaking into' are two nested container signals, the first inside the second; the final 'in' only joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the grand royal palace near Paris built by Louis XIV.

clue.text: Get out of boat in which one's messing about

indicators.note: messing about means jumbling things around, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Climb out of a boat in which someone is fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing about' rearranges BOAT IN; 'which one's' only links. 'Get out of' looks like 'leave', but means extract.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something out of someone is to extract or acquire it from them.

clue.text: A grave old doctor that could be the death of thousands

definitions.text: that could be the death of thousands

parts.note: a tomb is a grave
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: An old doctor's mistakes could send thousands to their graves.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon of this kind can kill vast numbers in one blast.

clue.text: Shame about short time available for book

indicators.note: the word for shame goes about, round, the time abbreviation

parts.note: alas is a cry of regret, like 'what a shame'
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It's a pity there's so little time left for reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside ALAS; 'available for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of maps is a reference book.

clue.text: Sea no good to a jellyfish, for example

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
US stands for unserviceable, meaning useless
taken as written

explanation.surface: The sea is useless to a jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only joins. US for useless (unserviceable) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A medusa is the free-swimming bell form of a cnidarian, typified by the jellyfish.

clue.text: Marry one's sweetheart

parts.note: a unit is a single one
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone weds the person they love.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetheart is read as 'sweet's heart', the middle letter of SWEET; ''s' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To join two people in wedlock is to bring them together.

clue.text: Notice Lady Macbeth wanted to get out

definitions.text: Lady Macbeth wanted to get out
definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's play she cries 'Out, damned ...!' while sleepwalking, trying to wash away a bloodstain

explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to notice; the bloodstain Lady Macbeth cannot scrub off is her famous spot.

clue.text: A pastoral poem mostly about girl

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the shortened poem is read backwards
mostly means most of the word but not all, so its last letter goes

parts.note: an idyll is a short poem of rural life
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country-life poem is mostly about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the poem's last letter and 'about' turns what remains; the clue's A then goes at the end. 'about' looks like 'concerning' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name.

clue.text: Ad-libbing is out! That's better

definitions.note: better as a verb; the answer is its -ing form

indicators.note: the word is is out, removed from the longer word

parts.note: improvising is speaking without a script, ad-libbing

explanation.surface: A performer is told to stop ad-libbing because things are going well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' takes IS from IMPROVISING. 'That's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something superior, enhancing it, is bettering it.

clue.text: Demanding chap should overlap rope

indicators.note: the two words share a letter where they meet, so one copy of it goes

parts.note: a string is a thin rope or cord
a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A demanding man insists ropes be laid overlapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should overlap' means STRING and GENT share their G, so it appears once.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict, exacting standards are severe and demanding.

clue.text: Thucydides' first piece of writing

definitions.meaning: the Greek historian's name begins with the Greek letter for th
a letter, a single written character

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek the name of the historian begins with this letter, and a letter is a written character.
